newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Mark,dlr in focus on slow Hungary BCE FX futures.
newsitem.headline: Mark,dlr in focus on slow Hungary BCE FX futures.

text.p: Hungary's foreign currency futures markets saw modest turnover dominated by deals in the mark and dollar, dealers said.
Total turnover of foreign currency futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) was 1.44 billion forints, down from Thursday's 2.09 million.
The mark and dollar were in focus with half of all turnover in September basket deals involving both currencies.

Basket deals are seen as a means of hedging against future large fluctuations of the dollar/mark and are based on the central bank's currency basket against which the forint is devalued by 1.1 percent per month.
The basket is made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
The September mark rose 0.19 to 112.20 forints, while dollar futures for the same month were also slightly up, by 0.10 to 191.50.
Significant interest remained for deferred maturities in the yen, whose low interest rates dealers believe make it a good long-term hedge against the devaluing forint.
The December yen saw significant turnover, falling 0.20 to 161.80 per 100 yen.
The central bank quoted the three currencies in its midday fix at 105.13 forints to the mark, up 0.19, 180.44 for the dollar, up 0.77, and 143.30 per 100 yen, up 0.85.
